title: Status Epilepticus (Convulsive)
summary: Convulsive seizure ≥5 min, or recurrent seizures without recovery — benzodiazepine now, escalate on a timed pathway.

sources.label: NICE NG217 — Epilepsies in children, young people and adults

blocks.title: Escalate immediately if
blocks.body: Seizure continues after two benzodiazepine doses, airway compromise, hypoxia despite oxygen, suspected eclampsia (give magnesium — call obstetrics), or first presentation with fever/meningism.

items: Start a clock; protect from injury; do not restrain or put anything in the mouth
Airway adjunct if tolerated, recovery position when practical, high-flow oxygen
Check capillary glucose immediately — treat hypoglycaemia (e.g. IV glucose per local policy)
IV access; bloods incl. glucose, U&E, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, FBC, anticonvulsant levels if on treatment
Ask: known epilepsy? alcohol? pregnancy? head injury? sepsis? drug overdose?

steps.detail: ABC, oxygen, glucose check, monitoring. Many seizures self-terminate before 5 min.
Lorazepam 4 mg slow IV. No IV access: midazolam 10 mg buccal, or diazepam 10 mg rectal — verify against local policy.
steps.branch: If alcohol excess suspected give IV thiamine (Pabrinex) alongside; if eclampsia possible give magnesium sulfate

steps.detail: If still seizing 5–10 min after the first dose: repeat lorazepam 4 mg IV once. Call for senior/anaesthetic support now.

Established status: levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4.5 g) IV, OR phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV with cardiac monitoring, OR sodium valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3 g) IV — choice per local policy and patient factors (avoid valproate in pregnancy/childbearing potential).
steps.branch: Already on one of these agents → prefer an alternative second-line drug

steps.detail: Anaesthetic induction and intubation (e.g. thiopental/propofol per anaesthetist), transfer to ICU, continuous EEG where available. Treat the cause.

blocks.title: Pearl
blocks.body: After the motor activity stops, ongoing coma may be non-convulsive status. If the patient does not begin to wake within 20–30 min of seizure termination, seek EEG and neurology advice.

blocks.title: Why the strict clock?
blocks.body: GABA-receptor internalisation begins within minutes of continuous seizure activity, so benzodiazepines lose effectiveness the longer the seizure runs, while excitotoxic neuronal injury and systemic complications accumulate. A timed, pre-planned escalation prevents the common failure mode: repeated small benzodiazepine doses given late.
